title: OR-D-03 callback reverse-mapping hijack: fixed in source, live testnet kernel still vulnerable
description: The uniqueness guard now exists in source: PutMiniApp asserts CallbackIndexMap[callbackContract] is null or already equals the same appId ("callback already registered", MorpheusOracle.Storage.cs:270-275), the stale-mapping delete is owner-checked (Storage.cs:258-262), and RebuildIndexes is admin-gated, bounded and first-wins/idempotent (MorpheusOracle.Requests.cs:153-183, guard at 174-178). However contracts/README.md:82-84 confirms the deployed testnet kernel 0xf54d8584ef82315c1800373272ab08ae0db2d5ef predates this fix: on the live chain any account can still register a fresh appId over another app's callback contract and repoint its legacy request routing (last-write-wins), a permissionless routing takeover / DoS against RequestFromCallback / Request / QueueAutomationRequest flows (MorpheusOracle.cs:1057-1094 resolve apps via FindMiniAppByCallback).
recommendation: Ship the pending ContractManagement.Update carrying the source fix to testnet (and verify mainnet kernel hash against the same source before/after upgrade), then run RebuildIndexes to backfill the reverse index; until deployed, treat callback-based routing on 0xf54d8584 as untrusted and prefer appId-direct SubmitMiniAppRequest paths.

title: ExpireStaleRequest inbox gap: fixed in source, live kernel still leaves inbox empty on expiry
description: Source now stores a canonical failed InboxItem and emits OnMiniAppInboxStored on expiry (MorpheusOracle.cs:842-861), matching the FulfillRequest shape (1151-1165). The deployed kernel (per contracts/README.md:93-96) refunds and emits RequestExpired/MiniAppRequestCompleted but writes no inbox item, so consumers that only poll GetInboxItem never observe the terminal state and wait indefinitely. No funds at risk (refund path is symmetric and clamped to the accrued pool, 802-822; sponsored-spend release at 831-834; reserved-fee release at 840); impact is consumer availability/liveness only, with a documented workaround (poll GetRequest().Status).
recommendation: Include in the same ContractManagement.Update as the OR-D-03 fix; until then document/enforce that consumers treat GetRequest().Status as the source of truth for terminal states.

title: Storage-prefix layout footgun: decimal-counted hex literals frozen on-chain
description: The prefix allocation block (MorpheusOracle.cs:64-93, definitions 94-143) documents that early prefixes were advanced as if counting in decimal (0x09 -> 0x10, 0x19 -> 0x20), leaving 0x0A-0x0F and 0x1A-0x1F skipped-but-free. Current assignments (0x01-0x2C) are collision-free in source, but the layout is frozen for the deployed contracts: any future edit that renumbers an existing prefix, or a contributor misreading the gaps as reserved, orphans live on-chain keys. Risk is process-level (upgrade-time data corruption), not an active bug.
recommendation: Keep the FOOTGUN comment; enforce append-only prefix allocation in review, add a source-assertion test pinning the full prefix map (alongside existing ContractSourceAssertions tests), and have the planned platform-library refactor reuse this exact map rather than re-deriving prefixes.

title: Keystore error swallow fixed; residual silent-fallback + ephemeral-key gate can still rotate oracle key without alarm
description: The oracle key-resolution chain now records configured and stable keystore failures before any development fallback, preserves the stable failure as the cause when no fallback is allowed, and rejects MORPHEUS_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_KEY when NODE_ENV=production. Regression tests cover both warning visibility and the production refusal. Live deployment and on-chain public-key continuity remain unverified.
recommendation: Deploy with a stable sealed key source, verify the published OracleEncryptionPublicKey against the worker key, and confirm warning/alert ingestion in the runtime environment.

title: Sandbox production enforcement: source and enclave configuration now fail closed
description: The retired SCRIPT_CHILD_ENABLE_PERMISSION_MODEL toggle no longer disables the sandbox. Both runners enable the Node permission model by default, reject wildcard/CIDR network allowlists, scrub child environments, and honor the explicit MORPHEUS_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED_CHILDREN escape hatch only outside production (permission-guard.js:72-129; script-runner.js:20-59; wasm-runner.js:20-57). The production container configuration now sets NODE_ENV=production in deploy/nitro/Dockerfile.enclave and the compose/service definitions, so the escape hatch is ignored in the intended enclave runtime. Source and unit tests verify the fail-closed branch; no deployed enclave runtime evidence has been captured in this report.
recommendation: Build and deploy the updated enclave image, then capture runtime evidence that child execArgv contains --permission and that MORPHEUS_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED_CHILDREN cannot remove it under NODE_ENV=production.

title: VRF host fallback now fails closed in production; enclave fulfillment remains deployment-gated
description: The random.generate lane still uses crypto.randomBytes(32) only for development/test environments, but executor.js:303-324 now rejects the relayer-local fallback whenever NODE_ENV=production. The enclave-attested path remains flag-gated by config.nitro.enclaveFulfill (executor.js:282-300), so production randomness requests fail with a terminal configuration error until MORPHEUS_RELAYER_ENCLAVE_FULFILL=1 is enabled and the enclave endpoint is verified. Source tests cover both the enclave route and the production refusal; no live deployment or on-chain consumer evidence has been captured in this report.
recommendation: Deploy with enclave fulfillment enabled only after verifying the attested endpoint and digest binding; until then keep random.generate disabled for production games rather than re-enabling the host fallback.

title: Durable-intake transient Supabase failures now fail closed in production
description: The request processors preserve persist-before-cursor-advance. Production now forces durableQueue.failClosed=true and disallows the local claim-backoff opt-in (config.js:87-105, 365-386). persistFreshEventsToDurableQueue now rethrows transient insert failures when failClosed is enabled after logging, so the discovery catch does not advance last_block or last_request_id; a focused regression test covers a Supabase 503. Non-production can still explicitly opt into local degraded behavior, and no deployed outage/recovery evidence has been captured in this report.
recommendation: Deploy the updated relayer with NODE_ENV=production, then exercise a controlled Supabase outage and verify the cursor remains unchanged until durable intake recovers.
